thread.title_full: Nassau authorizes $1 sale of Old Bethpage land to Oyster Bay - NewsBreak

author: Raymond Larsen
title: Nassau authorizes $1 sale of Old Bethpage land to Oyster Bay - NewsBreak
text:
By Raymond Larsen ,
10 hours ago The Theodore Roosevelt Executive and Legislative Building in Mineola, where the Nassau County Legislature meets. Nassau County lawmakers have authorized the sale of three small parcels in the hamlet of Old Bethpage to the Town of Oyster Bay for $1.
The county Legislature passed Ordinance 44-2026 on Sept. 28. It was approved unanimously by voice vote on the consent calendar, according to the Legislature's meeting video; Deputy Presiding Officer Thomas McKevitt moved the item and Legislator Delia DeRiggi-Whitton seconded it. The Legislature has not posted minutes of the meeting.
The land totals about 28,646 square feet and is listed on the county tax map as Section 47, Block E, Lots 749D, 749E and 766, in the Town of Oyster Bay, according to the ordinance. The town offered $1 for the property.
The ordinance authorizes the county executive to accept the town's offer and to sign the deed and contract of sale; it does not itself transfer the land. The county executive must still sign the deed and contract of sale. The ordinance took effect immediately.
Under the State Environmental Quality Review Act, the county found that the sale would "not have a significant effect on the environment and no further review is required," according to the ordinance.
The county Planning Commission, acting in an advisory capacity to the Legislature, recommended approving the release of Lots 749D and 749E on the condition that two trees be planted for each tree removed, and releasing Lot 766 without conditions, the ordinance says.
County documents do not say how the town plans to use the land.

Nassau County lawmakers have authorized the sale of three small parcels in the hamlet of Old Bethpage to the Town of Oyster Bay for $1. It was approved unanimously by voice vote on the consent calendar, according to the Legislature's meeting video; Deputy Presiding Officer Thomas McKevitt moved the item and Legislator Delia DeRiggi-Whitton seconded it.
